learn.hook: Fold a paper butterfly down the middle. Both wings match perfectly! That fold is magic: it is a line of symmetry.
points: A line of symmetry cuts a shape into two halves that match exactly, like mirror images.
If you fold along the line, one half sits exactly on the other.
Some shapes have many lines: a square has 4, an equilateral triangle has 3, a rectangle that is not a square has 2.
A circle has endless lines of symmetry: every line through its centre works.
Some shapes and letters have no line of symmetry, like the letters F and S.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
steps: Fold it down the middle (up and down): halves match
Fold it across the middle: halves match
Fold along each of the 2 corner-to-corner lines: halves match

learn.reallife: Rangolis, the Taj Mahal, leaves and butterflies all show lines of symmetry.

games.title: True or false?
items: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.
2 through the middles of the sides and 2 through the corners.
Every rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry.
A rectangle that is not a square has only 2.
The capital letter H has 2 lines of symmetry.
One up-down line and one across line.
A line of symmetry splits a shape into two matching halves.
Fold along it and the halves sit exactly on each other.
The capital letter F has a line of symmetry.
No fold of F makes the two halves match.

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square has 2 lines through the middles of its sides and 2 through its corners: 4 in all.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the corner-to-corner lines

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a rectangle that is not a square have?
quiz.explain: Only the up-down and across lines through the middle. The corner-to-corner lines do not work.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle has the same lines as a square

quiz.q: Which capital letter has a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: A has an up-down line of symmetry through its middle.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter that only looks balanced

quiz.q: Which capital letter has NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold of S makes the halves match. T, M and U each have an up-down line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a letter that looks the same after a turn must have a line of symmetry

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle (all sides equal) have?
quiz.explain: One line from each corner to the middle of the opposite side: 3 lines.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the up-down line

quiz.q: Riya folds a paper along a line and the two halves match exactly. What is the fold line called?
quiz.explain: A line that splits a shape into two matching halves is a line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a circle have?
options: Endless, any line through the centre
quiz.explain: Every line through the centre of a circle cuts it into two matching halves.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a circle has only an up-down and an across line

quiz.q: Which capital letter has exactly 2 lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: H has an up-down line and an across line. A has only an up-down line, E only an across line, and F has none.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one line

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'What is a line of symmetry? How do I find one?'
teach.praise: Flappy flap! Fold along the line and the two halves match. Like my wings!
teach.nudge: What do I do with the paper to test it? What happens to the two halves?

topics.title: Letter cut-outs: one fold or two

learn.hook: Fold a paper once, draw half of the letter A, cut, open — a whole A! Can you cut an H with two folds?
points: A letter with a vertical line of symmetry (A, M, T, U, V, W, Y) can be cut by folding once and drawing only half.
A letter with a horizontal line of symmetry (B, C, D, E, K) can be cut with a fold across the middle.
Letters with both lines (H, I, O, X) can be cut with two folds, drawing only a quarter.
Some letters (F, G, J, L, P, R) have no line of symmetry, so folding does not help.
The fold always becomes a line of symmetry of the cut-out.

example.q: Which letters can be cut with two folds, drawing just a quarter: H, A, E or X?
steps: Two folds need both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry
H and X have both
A has only vertical, E only horizontal

learn.reallife: Decorations for Diwali and school charts are often made by folding paper and cutting once.

games.title: Which line of symmetry?
items: A
T
M
B
E

H
X

games.title: Fold and cut
items: You can cut the letter T by folding once and drawing half.
T has a vertical line of symmetry.
You can cut F by folding.
F has no line of symmetry.
Two folds let you draw only a quarter of H.
H has a vertical and a horizontal line.
C has a vertical line of symmetry.
C has a horizontal line of symmetry.

quiz.q: Which letter can be cut out by folding once down the middle (vertical fold) and drawing half?
quiz.explain: V has a vertical line of symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter with a horizontal line

quiz.q: Which letter has a horizontal line of symmetry only?
quiz.explain: E matches top and bottom, but not left and right.
quiz.mistake: Confuses horizontal and vertical

quiz.q: Which letter has both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: X matches left-right and top-bottom.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any symmetric letter has both

quiz.q: To cut out the letter I with two folds, how much of it do you draw?
quiz.explain: Two folds make 4 layers, so you draw one quarter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every fold means half

quiz.q: Which letter cannot be made by folding and cutting, because it has no line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: G does not match itself on any fold line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every curved letter is symmetric

quiz.q: Ravi folds a paper once and cuts half a letter along the fold. He opens a perfect M. Where was the fold?
options: Down the middle of the M
Across the middle of the M
quiz.explain: M has a vertical line of symmetry, so the fold ran down its middle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the fold was across

quiz.q: How many of these letters have a vertical line of symmetry: A, U, W, S?
quiz.explain: A, U and W have one. S does not.
quiz.mistake: Counts S too

quiz.q: Which group has only letters with a horizontal line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: B, C and K each match top and bottom.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the lines

teach.ask: Gappu wants to cut out the letter H with as little drawing as possible. How should I fold the paper?
teach.praise: H has both lines of symmetry, so two folds and only a quarter to draw!
teach.nudge: Which lines of symmetry does H have?

learn.hook: Can you finish half a rangoli so it looks perfect? Let's make designs like an artist!
points: To complete a design with a mirror line, copy each part to the other side of the line.
Each point and its mirror image are the same distance from the line, on opposite sides.
On grid paper, count squares from the line to place the image exactly.
Fold-and-cut paper designs always have a line of symmetry along the fold.

example.q: On grid paper, a dot is 3 squares to the left of an up-down mirror line. Where does its mirror image go?
steps: Same distance from the line: 3 squares
Opposite side: right
example.answer: 3 squares to the right of the line, in the same row

learn.reallife: Kolam and rangoli artists, tailors and kite makers all build symmetrical designs.

items.text: A point and its mirror image are the same distance from the ___
A dot 4 squares left of an up-down mirror line has its image 4 squares to the ___ of the line
If half a design has 9 dots (none on the line), the whole design has ___ dots

games.title: Symmetrical or not?
items: A butterfly
Front view of the Taj Mahal
A heart shape
The letter A
The letter R
A random scribble
The letter G
The number 7

quiz.q: A dot is 2 squares to the left of an up-down mirror line. Where is its mirror image?
quiz.explain: The image is the same distance away on the other side: 2 squares to the right.
quiz.mistake: Puts the image on the same side, or doubles the distance

quiz.q: Meena folds a paper in half and cuts half a heart along the fold. What does she get when she opens it?
options: A full heart with a line of symmetry
quiz.explain: The fold becomes the line of symmetry, so both halves of the heart match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two halves come apart

quiz.q: Riya draws half a butterfly on one side of a mirror line. How should she finish it?
options: Draw the same half again, facing the same way
Draw the mirror image of the half on the other side
quiz.explain: The other half must be the flipped (mirror) copy, so the wings match.
quiz.mistake: Copies the half without flipping it

quiz.q: Which word looks exactly the same in a mirror placed beside it?
quiz.explain: M and O each have an up-down line of symmetry, and MOM reads the same both ways. D and B do not have an up-down line.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a word that reads the same both ways always looks the same in a mirror

quiz.q: Half a design touches an up-down mirror line and is 3 squares wide on its left. When it is completed, how wide is the whole design?
quiz.explain: The other half is also 3 squares wide: 3 + 3 = 6 squares.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the mirrored half

quiz.q: A rangoli has 8 equal petals around the centre. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
quiz.explain: Each petal moves to the next petal's place, 8 times in a full turn.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the 4 main directions

quiz.q: Joseph finishes a symmetrical dot design. The left half has 7 dots and no dot is on the line. How many dots are in the whole design?
quiz.explain: The right half mirrors the left: 7 + 7 = 14 dots.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one half

quiz.q: Harpreet makes a kite shape that is symmetrical about an up-down line. The left edge is 30 cm long. How long is the matching right edge?
quiz.explain: Mirror halves match exactly, so the right edge is also 30 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mirror half is half or double the size

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'How do I finish a design if I only have half of it?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Flip each part to the other side, the same distance from the line. Beautiful!
teach.nudge: How do I copy each part? How far from the line should it go?

learn.hook: Spin a pinwheel. It looks the same again and again before it finishes one full turn! That is turn symmetry.
points: Some designs look exactly the same after a part of a full turn. This is turn (rotational) symmetry.
Count how many times a design looks the same in one full turn.
A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn, after every 90°.
An equilateral triangle looks the same 3 times (every 120°). A rectangle that is not a square looks the same 2 times (every 180°).
Letters like S, N and Z look the same after a half turn (180°).

example.q: A ceiling fan has 3 equal blades. What is the smallest turn after which it looks the same?
steps: It looks the same 3 times in a full turn

learn.reallife: Fans, wheels, flowers, rangolis and chakra designs show turn symmetry.

games.title: Smallest turn to look the same
True or false?
items: The letter S looks the same after a half turn.
Turn S upside down and it is still S.
The letter A looks the same after a half turn.
After a half turn, A is upside down.
A square looks the same after a quarter turn.
A quarter turn is 90°, and a square looks the same every 90°.
A fan with 3 equal blades looks the same after a 90° turn.
It looks the same every 120°, not 90°.
A rectangle that is not a square looks the same after a half turn.
After 180° the long sides are back in place.

quiz.q: A ceiling fan has 3 equal blades. After what smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: It looks the same 3 times in one full turn: 360° ÷ 3 = 120°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every shape repeats after a quarter turn

quiz.q: A square looks the same after what smallest turn?
quiz.explain: A square looks the same 4 times in a full turn: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a square needs a half turn

quiz.q: Which capital letter looks the same after a half turn?
quiz.explain: Turn N upside down and it is still N. A, T and V end up upside down.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up turn symmetry with a mirror line

quiz.q: How many times does a square look the same during one full turn?
quiz.mistake: Counts only the half turn and full turn

quiz.q: A rectangle that is not a square looks the same after what smallest turn?
quiz.explain: After a quarter turn the long sides stand up, so it looks different. After a half turn (180°) it looks the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle behaves like a square

quiz.q: A flower rangoli has 6 equal petals around the centre. After what smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: It looks the same 6 times in a full turn: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Divides 360 by the wrong number

quiz.q: A star has 5 equal points. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
quiz.explain: Each point moves to the next point's place, so it looks the same 5 times.
quiz.mistake: Counts the corners inside and outside (10)

quiz.q: Which of these does NOT look the same after a quarter turn (90°)?
options: Rectangle that is not a square
quiz.explain: A long rectangle turned 90° stands on its short side, so it looks different.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all four-sided shapes act like squares

teach.ask: Gappu spins round and round: 'What is turn symmetry?'
teach.praise: Wheee! If a design looks the same before a full turn ends, it has turn symmetry!
teach.nudge: What do I do to the design? What must I see before the full turn is over?

learn.hook: Spin a paper firki slowly. At which turns does it look exactly as it started?
points: To test rotational symmetry, mark the centre, then turn the design by 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and a full turn.
A 4-blade windmill looks the same after every 1/4 turn.
Some designs match after a 1/2 turn but NOT after a 1/4 turn — like a rectangle or the letter S.
A shape can have rotational symmetry without any line of symmetry, like a windmill whose blades all bend the same way, or the letters S, N, Z.
Every shape looks the same after a full turn, so we only count smaller turns as rotational symmetry.

example.q: A rectangle (not a square) is turned. At which of 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 turn does it look the same?
steps: 1/4 turn: it is now standing up — different
1/2 turn: same
3/4 turn: standing up again — different
example.answer: Only at the 1/2 turn (and the full turn)

learn.reallife: Fans, wheels, flowers and windmills all have rotational symmetry.

games.title: Looks the same after a 1/4 turn?
items: Square
4-blade windmill
Plus sign +
Rectangle (not square)
Letter S
Letter N
Letter Z
Letter H

games.title: Turn facts
items: A 4-blade firki looks the same after a 1/4 turn.
Each blade moves into the next blade's place.
The letter Z looks the same after a 1/4 turn.
Z matches only after a 1/2 turn.
A shape can have rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry.
Like a firki with bent blades, or the letter S.
Every design looks the same after a full turn.
A full turn brings it back to the start.

quiz.q: A paper windmill has 4 blades. After which smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: Each 1/4 turn moves every blade into the next blade's place.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only a half turn works

quiz.q: A rectangle that is not a square is turned. At which turn does it first look the same?
quiz.explain: After a 1/4 turn it stands on its short side. After a 1/2 turn it matches.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle acts like a square

quiz.q: Which letter looks the same after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn?
quiz.explain: N turned upside down is still N, but a 1/4 turn lays it on its side. A and T change after a 1/2 turn; + already matches after a 1/4 turn.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter that matches after every 1/4 turn

quiz.q: Which shape has rotational symmetry but NO line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: S matches after a 1/2 turn, but no fold line makes its halves match.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rotation and reflection always go together

quiz.q: How many times does a 4-blade windmill look the same in one full turn (counting the full turn)?
quiz.explain: At 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 and the full turn: 4 times.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the half turn

quiz.q: A design matches after a 1/2 turn. Must it also match after a 1/4 turn?
quiz.explain: A rectangle matches after a 1/2 turn but not after a 1/4 turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks matching at 1/2 means matching at 1/4

quiz.q: Which test checks rotational symmetry?
options: Fold it and see if the halves match
Turn it about its centre and see if it looks the same before a full turn
quiz.explain: Rotational symmetry is about turning, not folding.
quiz.mistake: Confuses turning with folding

quiz.q: A firki has 3 blades all bent the same way. Which is true?
options: It looks the same after a 1/3 turn but has no line of symmetry
It looks the same only after a full turn
It has a line of symmetry but no turn symmetry
quiz.explain: The bent blades spoil every fold line, but turning by 1/3 moves each blade to the next.
quiz.mistake: Thinks all turn designs have fold lines

teach.ask: Gappu's firki has 4 blades bent the same way. Does it have a line of symmetry? Does it have turn symmetry?
teach.praise: No fold line works, but it looks the same after every 1/4 turn!
teach.nudge: What happens when I fold it? And when I turn it?

learn.hook: Turn your notebook upside down: 69 is still 69! Which other numbers can do tricks like this?
points: Digits written in a simple way: 0 and 8 have a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry, and look the same after a 1/2 turn.
3 has a horizontal line of symmetry only. 1 written as a straight stick has both lines and a 1/2-turn symmetry.
6 turned by a 1/2 turn becomes 9, so 69 and 96 look the same after a 1/2 turn — but they have no line of symmetry.
Numbers like 11, 88, 808 and 1001 (with stick 1s) have a vertical line, a horizontal line and 1/2-turn symmetry.
To create a number with 1/2-turn symmetry, use 0, 1, 8 in matching places, or pair 6 with 9.

example.q: Does 808 look the same after a 1/2 turn? Does it have a vertical line of symmetry?
steps: Turned upside down, 808 reads 808
A mirror down the middle gives 8-0-8 again

learn.reallife: Some digital clock times like 10:01 look the same in a mirror. Car number plates can hide symmetry too!

games.title: Digit facts
items: 8 has a horizontal line of symmetry.
Its top and bottom halves match.
3 has a vertical line of symmetry.
3 has only a horizontal line.
6 turned by a 1/2 turn looks like 9.
That is why 69 stays 69.
0 looks the same after a 1/2 turn.
Turned upside down, it is still 0.
7 has a line of symmetry.
7 does not match on any fold.

quiz.q: Which digit has a horizontal line of symmetry but no vertical one?
quiz.explain: 3's top and bottom halves match, but its left and right do not.
quiz.mistake: Picks a digit with both lines

quiz.q: Which digit has both a vertical and a horizontal line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: 8 matches left-right and top-bottom.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3 has a vertical line

quiz.q: Which number looks the same after a 1/2 turn?
quiz.explain: Turning 69 upside down: 6 becomes 9 and 9 becomes 6, and their order flips, giving 69 again.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 66 stays 66 — it becomes 99

quiz.q: Does 69 have a line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: No fold makes 69 match itself, but a 1/2 turn does.
quiz.mistake: Thinks turn symmetry means a fold line too

quiz.q: Which number (with stick 1s) has a vertical line, a horizontal line and 1/2-turn symmetry?
quiz.explain: 1001 matches in a mirror, top to bottom, and upside down.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every palindrome is symmetric

quiz.q: Which 3-digit number has 1/2-turn symmetry?
quiz.explain: 808 turned upside down is still 808. 880 becomes 088.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the order flips in a 1/2 turn

quiz.q: Which 4-digit number looks the same after a 1/2 turn?
quiz.explain: Turned upside down, 6889 becomes 6889: the 9 at the end becomes a 6 at the front.
quiz.mistake: Does not flip the order of digits

quiz.q: Which number has a horizontal line of symmetry only (not vertical)?
quiz.explain: Each 3 matches top-bottom, but 33 does not match left-right in a mirror.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 3 has a vertical line

teach.ask: Gappu wants a 2-digit number that looks the same upside down but has no line of symmetry. Can you help?
teach.praise: 69! A half turn changes 6 into 9 and 9 into 6, so it stays 69!
teach.nudge: What happens to 6 when it is turned upside down?

learn.hook: Can you colour a 3 by 3 square with just two colours so it looks the same after every quarter turn?
points: To test a design for rotational symmetry, trace it, turn the tracing about the centre, and check if it fits.
To make a design match after a 1/2 turn, every shape must have a partner exactly opposite through the centre.
For a 1/4-turn match, every shape needs partners in all four quarter positions.
Lines of reflection symmetry are drawn where folding makes the halves match. A design may have several.
In a 3 × 3 grid, colouring the 4 corners one colour and the 4 edge squares another gives a 1/4-turn match.

example.q: A design has a red dot at the top. What must you add so it matches after a 1/2 turn?
steps: A 1/2 turn moves the top to the bottom
So add a red dot at the bottom, the same distance from the centre
example.answer: A red dot at the bottom

learn.reallife: Rangolis, kolams and tile floors are planned so they match after turns and folds.

items.text: A dot at the top; for a 1/2-turn match add one at the ___
A dot at the top; for a 1/4-turn match add dots at the right, bottom and ___
3 × 3 grid with 1/4-turn symmetry: corners one colour, ___ squares another
A square design can have up to ___ lines of symmetry

games.title: Design checks
items: If every shape has a partner opposite through the centre, the design matches after a 1/2 turn.
A 1/2 turn swaps partners.
A design with a dot only at the top matches after a 1/4 turn.
After the turn, the dot is on the right.
Colouring a 2 × 2 grid with two colours can give a 1/4-turn match.
A 1/4 turn moves every cell to the next, so all four must be one colour.
Tracing paper helps test rotational symmetry.
Turn the tracing and see if it fits.

quiz.q: A design has one star at the top. Where must another star go so the design matches after a 1/2 turn?
quiz.explain: A 1/2 turn sends the top to the bottom.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a 1/2 turn goes to the side

quiz.q: A design has a dot at the top. Which dots must be added for it to match after every 1/4 turn?
quiz.explain: Each 1/4 turn moves the dot to the next side: right, bottom, left.
quiz.mistake: Adds only the opposite dot

quiz.q: How can you test a design for rotational symmetry?
options: Trace it and turn the tracing about the centre
quiz.explain: Turning the tracing shows whether the design fits itself before a full turn.
quiz.mistake: Uses a fold, which tests reflection

quiz.q: In a 3 × 3 grid, how can two colours be used so it looks the same after every 1/4 turn?
options: 4 corners one colour, 4 edge squares the other
Top row one colour, the rest the other
Left column one colour, the rest the other
quiz.explain: Corners turn into corners and edges into edges, so this matches.
quiz.mistake: Colours a row, which moves to a column after a turn

quiz.q: A square rangoli has the same pattern on every side. How many lines of symmetry can it have at most?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 lines: 2 through opposite corners and 2 through the middles of opposite sides.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the up-down and across lines

quiz.q: Which change makes this design match after a 1/2 turn: a triangle on the left only?
options: Add a triangle at the top
Remove the triangle and add a circle at the top
Add a square on the left
Add the same triangle on the right, turned upside down
quiz.explain: A 1/2 turn moves the left triangle to the right and turns it upside down, so that is the partner it needs.
quiz.mistake: Adds the partner in the wrong place

quiz.q: A design looks the same after a 1/4 turn. Does it also look the same after a 1/2 turn?
options: Yes, because two 1/4 turns make a 1/2 turn
Only if it is a circle
quiz.explain: If it matches after one 1/4 turn, it matches after two of them as well.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each turn must be checked from scratch

quiz.q: A design has a line of symmetry going down the middle. What does that mean?
options: Folding along it makes the two halves match
Turning it by 1/4 makes it match
quiz.explain: A line of symmetry is a fold line where the halves match.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a fold line with a turn

teach.ask: Gappu drew a flower petal pointing up. How do I finish it so it looks the same after every quarter turn?
teach.praise: I add petals pointing right, down and left — 4 petals in all!
teach.nudge: Where does the petal go after a quarter turn?

learn.hook: Take squares and equilateral triangles with the same side length. Join them to make star and flower designs!
points: Squares and equilateral triangles with equal sides fit neatly edge to edge.
A square with a triangle on each of its 4 sides makes a star with 4 lines of symmetry and 1/4-turn symmetry.
A square with a triangle on just one side has 1 line of symmetry but no rotational symmetry.
A square with triangles on two opposite sides has 2 lines of symmetry and 1/2-turn symmetry.
Sort designs: reflection only, rotation only, or both.

example.q: A square has triangles on its top and bottom sides. Which symmetries does it have?
steps: Up-down and left-right folds both match: 2 lines
A 1/2 turn swaps the top and bottom triangles: matches
A 1/4 turn puts the triangles at the sides: no match

learn.reallife: Mosaics in temples and mosques often join squares and triangles into beautiful symmetric stars.

games.title: Sort the design
items: Square + 1 triangle on top
Square + triangles on all 4 sides
Square + triangles on top and bottom
Square + triangles on top and right
Triangle + square on its base
Hexagon of 6 triangles

quiz.q: A square has an equilateral triangle on each of its 4 sides. How many lines of symmetry?
quiz.explain: The star matches on both diagonal folds and both middle folds: 4 lines.
quiz.mistake: Counts only up-down and across

quiz.q: That 4-triangle star is turned. After which smallest turn does it look the same?
quiz.explain: Each 1/4 turn moves every triangle to the next side.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only a 1/2 turn works

quiz.q: A square has a triangle on its top side only. What symmetry does it have?
options: 1 line of symmetry, no turn symmetry
quiz.explain: Folding down the middle matches, but any turn moves the triangle away.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every design has turn symmetry

quiz.q: A square has triangles on the top and bottom. Does it look the same after a 1/2 turn?
quiz.explain: A 1/2 turn swaps the top and bottom triangles, so it matches.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only stars match

quiz.q: Does that same design (triangles on top and bottom) match after a 1/4 turn?
quiz.explain: After a 1/4 turn the triangles are on the left and right.
quiz.mistake: Thinks matching at 1/2 means matching at 1/4

quiz.q: Six equilateral triangles meet at a point to form a hexagon. How many times does it look the same in one full turn?
quiz.explain: Every 1/6 turn moves each triangle into the next place: 6 times.
quiz.mistake: Counts the lines of the hexagon wrongly

quiz.q: A square has triangles on its top and right sides. Which is true?
options: It has 1 line of symmetry (a diagonal) and no turn symmetry
quiz.explain: The fold along the diagonal between top and right swaps the two triangles. No turn matches.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two triangles always give 2 lines

quiz.q: Which design has BOTH reflection and rotational symmetry?
options: Square with triangles on top and right
Square with triangles on all 4 sides
Triangle with a square on one side
quiz.explain: The 4-triangle star has 4 lines and 1/4-turn symmetry.
quiz.mistake: Picks a design with only a fold line

teach.ask: Gappu put one triangle on the top of a square. How can I change it so it looks the same after a half turn?
teach.praise: I add a triangle at the bottom — then a half turn matches!
teach.nudge: Where does the top triangle go after a half turn?

learn.hook: In Rajasthan, craftspeople carve wooden blocks and stamp them on cloth. Turn the block and stamp again — a pattern appears!
points: A block print is a mirror image of the carved block, like a stamp.
Printing a block 4 times around a centre, turning it a 1/4 turn each time, makes a design with 1/4-turn symmetry.
Printing it twice with a 1/2 turn gives a design with 1/2-turn symmetry.
Border shapes repeat along a line. Some have reflection symmetry (like ▲ or ♥), some have rotational symmetry (like S or Z), some have both (like X or ◆).
You can print your own patterns with blocks cut from vegetables like potato or lady's finger.

example.q: A block makes an L-shaped print. You print it 4 times around a point, turning 1/4 each time. What symmetry does the design have?
steps: Each print is the last one turned by 1/4
So the whole design matches after a 1/4 turn

learn.reallife: Bagru and Sanganer in Rajasthan are famous for block printing. Lady's finger cut across makes a lovely star stamp!

games.title: Block printing facts
items: A print is a mirror image of the carving.
Like a rubber stamp.
Printing 4 times with 1/4 turns gives 1/4-turn symmetry.
Each print is the next one turned.
Printing twice with a 1/2 turn always gives 4 lines of symmetry.
It gives 1/2-turn symmetry; lines depend on the block.
Lady's finger cut across makes a star-like print.
Its cross-section has ridges around a centre.

quiz.q: A carved block shows the letter F facing right. Which way does the print face?
quiz.explain: Stamping flips the carving, so the print is its mirror image.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the print copies the block exactly

quiz.q: A block is printed 4 times around a centre, turned by a 1/4 turn each time. What symmetry does the design have?
quiz.explain: Each print is the previous one turned by 1/4, so the whole design matches after a 1/4 turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks turning the block spoils the symmetry

quiz.q: A block is printed twice with a 1/2 turn between prints. After which turn does the design match?
quiz.explain: The two prints swap places after a 1/2 turn.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it matches after a 1/4 turn

quiz.q: How many times must you print a block, turning 1/4 each time, to complete a 1/4-turn design?
quiz.explain: Four quarter turns make a full turn, so 4 prints.
steps: 4 × 1/4 = 1 full turn
quiz.mistake: Thinks two prints are enough

quiz.q: Which border shape has rotational symmetry but no line of symmetry?
quiz.explain: Z matches after a 1/2 turn but has no fold line.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape with a fold line

quiz.q: Which border shape has both reflection and rotational symmetry?
quiz.explain: X has fold lines and also matches after a 1/2 turn.
quiz.mistake: Picks a shape with only one kind

quiz.q: Which border shape has reflection symmetry only?
quiz.explain: A heart matches when folded down the middle, but not after a 1/2 turn.
quiz.mistake: Picks a rotating letter

quiz.q: Which vegetable, cut across, gives a print with many matching parts around a centre?
options: A long bean cut along its length
quiz.explain: Bhindi cut across shows ridges all around its centre, like a star.
quiz.mistake: Picks a cut that has no centre pattern

teach.ask: Gappu has a potato block shaped like a leaf. How can I print a design that looks the same after every quarter turn?
teach.praise: I print the leaf 4 times around a centre, turning it a quarter each time!
teach.nudge: How many prints and how much turning do I need?
